json-output.md lines 25-26 and 47-49 say a per-site NDJSON line omits exitCode, while `cairn health <site>` writes a site payload that carries it (line 149). The rule for telling the two forms apart is stated, and the wrapper also knows which command it ran.

cli-cairn-exit-codes.md lines 91-97 say empty stdout under --json means no payload was written, and each such case reports UNKNOWN (exit 3). No documented case pairs empty --json stdout with any other code, so the pages leave nothing to guess.

cli-cairn-exit-codes.md lines 79-81 say a cancelled run and a tool fault report UNKNOWN (exit 3), and json-output.md lines 50-52 say a signal-cut site is folded into the summary. In the code, health_sweep.go:111-112 returns an error, a tool fault, before any summary is written. The only remaining case is a process killed from outside, and cairn cannot document that exit code.
Keeping timestamps as strings is a representation choice, and it rests on what json-output.md line 116 states. The item claims no defect.

The exit-codes page (lines 8, 63) says an --expect-sites mismatch exits 3. json-output.md lines 300-302 describe `errors` only as registry reads that could not complete, and no published page says whether a mismatch writes a payload. The code does write one: sites.go:80-81 appends ErrExpectSites to listErrs and writeSites (sites.go:140-153) marshals it into `errors`.

json-output.md lines 386-388 say the only password prompt belongs to `cairn auth set`, which is not a --json command. No --json command is documented as reading stdin, and the job did not need this fact to parse output.

json-output.md lines 346-348 say `adoptable` was added within schema version 1 and that a reader written before it still reads every candidate. The candidate schema (cairn-adopt-list.schema.json line 20) is closed with additionalProperties:false, and the page calls the payloads a closed contract (line 8), so a validator that follows the normative schema's closedness would reject the added field. The docs never state a forward-compatibility policy that reconciles the two.

This is not a contradiction. The doctor schema's state enum (line 28) lists the shared frozen state words (json-output.md line 508), and json-output.md line 402 says doctor never writes `held`. A schema that permits a value the producer never emits does not differ from the page on what gets written.

This is not a contradiction. The doctor schema (lines 22, 38) sets a minimum requirement, and cli-cairn-doctor.md lines 95 and 109 describe what the producer always writes. Both hold together: the doctor json.go:47,54 emits condition and fix as optional fields, which conforms to the schema.

This is not a contradiction. The auth-check schema (lines 19-25) makes `reason` optional, and json-output.md line 376 says the producer writes it beside every non-pass row. A looser schema that still accepts the stated output does not conflict with the page.
